framework.summary: The bill requires no new framework; it verifies compliance with a framework required by existing law.

transparency_report.summary: The third party verifier, not the developer, must publish a summary of its compliance report within 60 days; the developer must link to it on its website within 15 days.
transparency_report.quote: The third party verifier shall conspicuously publish a summary of the verifier's report within sixty days of such report's completion.

incident_reporting.summary: The bill adds no incident reporting duty.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must each year engage a third party verifier to report on their compliance with their own framework; from January 1, 2029 the verifier must be state accredited.

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protections.

registration.summary: No registration of developers; the state office only accredits third party verifiers.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: The bill defines no compute threshold.

revenue_threshold.summary: The bill defines no revenue threshold.

harm_threshold.summary: The bill defines no harm threshold.

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may sue for up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 per later violation, including failing to obtain the verification.
